questions.question: For a random variable $X$ with finite variance and $\mathbb{E}[X]\ne0$, which expression defines the squared coefficient of variation $C_X^2$?

A service time $S$ with positive mean and finite variance is recorded in hours and has $C_s^2=0.4$. The same service times are converted to minutes, giving $60S$. What is the squared coefficient of variation of $60S$?
A service time $S$ is exponentially distributed with rate $\mu>0$, so its mean is $1/\mu$. What is its squared coefficient of variation $C_s^2$?
For a random variable $X$ with finite variance and $\mathbb{E}[X]>0$, when is its squared coefficient of variation $C_X^2$ equal to $0$?
options: Exactly when $X$ equals a constant with probability one
Exactly when the standard deviation of $X$ is below $1$
Never, because the scv of a random variable is always positive

questions.question: A service time $S$ has mean $\mathbb{E}[S]=3$ minutes and squared coefficient of variation $C_s^2=\operatorname{Var}(S)/(\mathbb{E}[S])^2=2$. Which interpretation of this value is correct?
options: The standard deviation of $S$ is twice its mean, so $6$ minutes
The variance of $S$ is twice its mean, so $6$ minutes squared
Relative to its mean, $S$ is more variable than any exponential time
The value is invalid, as an scv always lies between $0$ and $1$

questions.question: A service time has mean $4$ minutes and standard deviation $2$ minutes. What is its squared coefficient of variation $C_s^2$?
A service time is uniformly distributed on $[0,10]$ minutes. What is its squared coefficient of variation $C_s^2$?
The number of calls arriving at a help desk per day is Poisson distributed with mean $25$. What is the squared coefficient of variation of this daily count?
Only the first two moments of a service time $S$ are known: $\mathbb{E}[S]=2$ minutes and $\mathbb{E}[S^2]=10$ minutes squared. Which value does its scv $C_s^2$ take?
A service consists of $4$ consecutive phases whose durations are independent and each exponential with mean $2$ minutes. What is the squared coefficient of variation of the total service time?

Two service times $A$ and $B$ have positive means and finite variances, and $\operatorname{Var}(A)>\operatorname{Var}(B)$; nothing is known about the means. What can be concluded about their scvs $C_A^2$ and $C_B^2$?
options: $C_A^2>C_B^2$, since a larger variance means a larger scv
$C_A^2>C_B^2$, provided both are measured in the same unit
$C_A^2<C_B^2$, since a larger variance comes with a larger mean
Either order is possible, since each scv also depends on its mean

questions.question: Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process with on average $30$ arrivals per week, so the weekly arrival count has scv $1/30$. What is $C_a^2$, the scv of the inter-arrival times?

Two discrete-time queues receive the same arrival stream, with on average $6$ jobs per period. In queue 1 the capacity per period is $9.75$ with probability $2/3$ and $0$ otherwise; in queue 2 it is $19.5$ with probability $1/3$ and $0$ otherwise. Which statement about drift and queue lengths is correct?
options: Queue 2 has the larger drift, because its capacity is more variable
The queue lengths behave alike, because the two drifts are equal
The drift is equal, yet queue 2 shows larger queue-length fluctuations
Queue 2 has shorter queues, as a capacity of $19.5$ clears long queues

questions.question: A capacity $X$ with mean $\mu=4$ and scv $c^2=3$ is to be modelled as $X=bB$ with $B\sim\operatorname{Bern}(p)$, $b>0$ and $0<p\le1$. Which choice of $p$ and $b$ gives this mean and scv?
The capacity per period of a server is uniformly distributed on $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$ jobs. What is the squared coefficient of variation of this capacity?

In each period an arrival occurs with probability $0.2$, independently of other periods. Let $T$ be the number of periods up to and including the next arrival, so $T\sim\operatorname{FS}(0.2)$. What is $C_T^2$?
For which of these random variables $X$ is the squared coefficient of variation $C_X^2$ undefined?
A service time $S$ has mean $\mathbb{E}[S]=2$ minutes and squared coefficient of variation $C_s^2=1$. Which conclusion about $S$ is justified?
options: $\operatorname{Var}(S)=4$, and the distribution of $S$ is not determined by these two numbers
$\operatorname{Var}(S)=2$, and the distribution of $S$ is not determined by these two numbers

questions.question: With probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$ a job needs no processing (service time $0$); otherwise its service time is exponential with mean $2$ minutes. What is the squared coefficient of variation of the service time?
Each service consists of a fixed setup of $1$ minute followed by an exponential processing time with mean $2$ minutes. What is the squared coefficient of variation of the total service time?
